import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 218

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/218](https://www.erdosproblems.com/218)
-/

namespace Erdos218

/--
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is followed by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_218.variants.le : {n | primeGap n ≤ primeGap (n + 1)}.HasDensity <| 1 / 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is preceded by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_218.variants.ge : {n | primeGap (n + 1) ≤ primeGap n}.HasDensity <| 1 / 2 := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many indices $n$ such that the prime gap at $n$ is equal to the prime gap
at $n+1$. This is equivalent to the existence of infinitely many arithmetic progressions of
length $3$, see `erdos_141.variants.infinite_three`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_218.variants.infinite_equal_prime_gap : {n | primeGap n = primeGap (n + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos218

findings.description: The equivalence claimed in the docstring (lines 45–46) omits the qualifier “of consecutive primes”: it says only “infinitely many arithmetic progressions of length 3.” Unrestricted three-term arithmetic progressions are trivially infinite; the intended equivalent statement concerns progressions consisting of three consecutive primes. The Lean theorem itself correctly states the equal-prime-gaps conjecture.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/218 conjectures infinitely many n with d_{n+1} = d_n. The linked source https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/141 explicitly concerns “consecutive primes in arithmetic progression” and says that infinitude remains open even for k = 3, distinguishing this from progressions of primes that need not be consecutive.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to say “infinitely many arithmetic progressions of length 3 consisting of consecutive primes.” No change to the Lean proposition is needed.

review.notes: All three formal propositions faithfully match the cited source; no mathematical misformalization or stale status was found. The source still records the problem as open. Erdős Problems pages were read through r.jina.ai after direct requests returned HTTP 403. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without errors or warnings: they confirm real-valued natural density, the harmless zero denominator at the initial cutoff, the first prime gaps, positivity of every prime gap, and the equivalence between equal adjacent gaps and the three-term arithmetic-progression equation. Zero-based prime indexing preserves both density and infinitude.
